thread:
lina: Heads up — APAC pool-7 (4090) has a sustained ECC correctable rate spike, ~5x baseline over the last 12h. Seeing clusters of cards with intermittent bursts, not single-card constant noise. Thinking we should define a hot-swap / isolation playbook + a regional circuit-breaker to avoid cascade.

ops-bot: [ALERT] pool=apac-pool-7 metric=ecc_correctables rate=271/hr threshold=60/hr window=1h

alex: Can you paste the query and the card-level breakdown? need to see whether it's concentrated on a few cards or evenly spread.

lina: Query I used:
```sql
SELECT card_id, sum(correctables) as c, max(per_min) as peak_p FROM telemetry.ecc_events
WHERE pool='apac-pool-7' AND ts > now()-interval '12 hours'
GROUP BY card_id ORDER BY c DESC LIMIT 40;
```
Top results show 6 cards with c>800, next 20 in 150-300 range.

morgan: Sounds like a small set of hot cards plus noise. Proposal: a 3-stage policy — monitor -> isolate (migrate new allocations off the card) -> hot-swap if sustained. Threshold ideas: per-card >500 correctables in 12h OR >120/hr sustained for 3 hours => mark for isolation. If isolated and rate remains >100/hr for 24h => schedule hot-swap.

jia: Agree with stages. Add a pool-level circuit-breaker: if >10% of active cards exceed isolation threshold within a pool OR pool-wide rate > 2x normal for 1h, trigger cross-region routing to avoid capacity exhaustion. That avoids blind evacs during regional flaps.

ralph: What about cost/ops impact of hot-swap? Field team needs heads-up/slot to physically replace cards. Can we prefer automated soft-isolate first and queue replacements during low-impact windows?

morgan: Yes — hot-swap should be scheduled with ops. We can automate the queuing: when a card moves to REPLACE_PENDING tag, it goes into a replace queue and we include metadata (severity, observed window, model placement impact). If severity=high (e.g., >2k correctables in 6h) mark as high-priority.

lina: Implementation notes: quick isolation can be done by updating placement policy: set card.state=quarantine and apply allocation-filter to drain new allocations. Example API call to flag card:
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
  https://api.redwood.internal/v1/infra/cards/mark
  -d '{"card_id":"GPU-APAC-37","state":"quarantine","reason":"ecc-spike"}'
```
That doesn't force-migrate running jobs but prevents new ones.

alex: For automated assessment, we should add a short ML-style filter to reduce noise: require >3 separate bursts spaced >10min OR a rolling stdev above baseline before triggering auto-isolate. Cuts false positives from transient kernel retries.

jia: Good call. Also add annotation to metrics with firmware/driver versions — correlated flaps have matched driver revs in past incidents. If many cards share same firmware, prefer fleet-wide mitigations (driver rollback) before mass replacement.

ralph: Ops action items: add a "replace window" calendar for EMEA/APAC with 4 slots/week; integrate replace queue so on-call can claim tasks. Also add a Slack alert channel for REPLACE_PENDING with card_id and severity.

morgan: For circuit-breaker behavior, fallback order: 1) reroute traffic to other regions (if capacity), 2) route to dedicated lower-performance model variant, 3) shed non-critical batch jobs. We should avoid wholesale draining unless replacement queue is backed up.

lina: Decision: adopt the 3-stage policy + regional circuit-breaker as described. I'll draft a short playbook and a minimal automator to flag cards with the ML filter. Action items:
- lina: write playbook draft and PR the isolator API by EOD tomorrow
- morgan: implement REPLACE_PENDING queue + priority tagging prototype by end of week
- alex: add rolling-stdev filter to alerting rules (short PR)
- jia: add firmware correlation column to ECC dashboard and driver-rollback checklist
- ralph: create replace-window calendar and ops-runbook stub

lina: Thanks — ping me if you want to sync on the playbook. :thumbsup:
